messages:
acme-devops: Hey team, our onprem installer fails when it tries to pull packages and model shards behind our corp proxy. Installer logs show TLS errors and 403 from model-registry. Can you share a minimal outbound-hosts checklist we can give infra to whitelist?
meera.s: Thanks for reporting — can you paste the failing log lines and confirm whether you’re using a transparent TLS proxy / MITM (Zscaler etc) or a strict outbound firewall?
acme-devops: Logs: 
```
ERROR: failed to fetch https://pypi.org/simple/requests/: TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
Model pull: GET https://models.redwood.ai/shard/abc123 -> 403
```
We are behind a corporate FW + TLS intercept (Zscaler).
alex.k: Okay. Two likely issues: (1) transparent TLS intercept altering certs/SNI -> OCSP/SNI fail, (2) firewall blocking specific IP ranges used by CDNs/model shard hosts.
meera.s: Quick repro steps for infra: 1) curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/health 2) openssl s_client -connect models.redwood.ai:443 -servername models.redwood.ai -status
Include these outputs. If intercept present, s_client will show a different issuer and OCSP stapling may be missing.
acme-devops: Ran curl -v, returns 200 but cert issuer is CorpCA and s_client shows no OCSP staple.
raul.eng: That confirms TLS intercept. For installer we require TLS passthrough (no MITM) for model shard downloads and auth flows — or you must add our CA to services that validate issuers (not recommended). Also ensure the proxy allows SNI to reach target FQDNs for split-horizon setups.
alex.k: To unblock quickly, infra can allowlist these FQDNs and ports (minimal):
- pypi.org (443)
- files.pythonhosted.org (443)
- models.redwood.ai (443)
- registry.redwood.ai (443)  # model registry auth/token endpoints
- telemetry-api.redwood.ai (443)
- auth.redwood.ai (443)  # OAuth/JWT introspect/token endpoints
- kms-us.redwood.ai (443)  # optional if using KMS integration
- storage-cdn.*.fastly.net (443) and relevant CDN CNAMES used by model shards

Note: if your proxy resolves split-horizon hostnames to internal IPs, allow DNS resolution to the real external FQDNs or bypass proxy for those hosts.
meera.s: Also allow outbound to these IP ranges (if firewall can only do IPs): 
- 52.86.0.0/15 (example CDN range)
- 151.101.0.0/16 (Fastly)
- 3.120.0.0/14 (cloud provider edge)
(ask infra to confirm with their CDN provider; IPs vary by region)
acme-devops: For ocsp/ocsp-staple, infra needs to allow access to OCSP responder hostnames?
raul.eng: Yes — TLS intercept breaks OCSP stapling. Best practice: allow TLS passthrough for these flows. If you can't, ensure the intercepting proxy supports OCSP stapling and preserves SNI, and that the proxy trusts our CA chain for backend cert validation.
alex.k: Example commands you can run to prove path works (share outputs):
- curl -v --resolve models.redwood.ai:443:52.86.10.123 https://models.redwood.ai/health
- openssl s_client -connect models.redwood.ai:443 -servername models.redwood.ai -status
- curl -I https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/ --max-time 10

If you want, we can provide a minimal hosts file with current CDN CNAMES we use for shards — but CDN backends change, so IP allowlisting is brittle.
meera.s: TL;DR for infra paste: allow outbound TCP 443 to the FQDNs listed above, bypass MITM for those FQDNs (or configure proxy to preserve SNI and OCSP). Also ensure egress DNS resolves public records for these hosts.
acme-devops: Thanks — I'll forward to infra with the curl/openssl commands. One more: do we need to allow any specific ports for installer telemetry/billing?
alex.k: Telemetry & billing use 443 only. If you use image/model shard downloads over insecure ports, we'll call that out, but default is 443.
sre-bot: note: created support ticket #S-38721 and assigned to eng-oncall for model-registry 403 follow-up.
meera.s: If infra replies with capture of the failing curl + s_client output, we can iterate. Happy to jump on a quick call with infra and your team to walk through trace if helpful. :thumbsup:
